The `root>low` element creates a new stacking context because it is positioned (`position: absolute`) and has a numerical `z-index` (1). Consequently, the `z-index: 999` of `root>low>inner` is scoped within `root>low` and does not affect its stack level relative to elements outside that context. Since `root>high` is a sibling of `root>low` and has a higher `z-index` (2 vs 1), `root>high` is rendered on top of `root>low` and all of its descendants.

ANSWER: root>high
